title: Cerebras CEO reveals the capacity shortfall behind OpenAI's turn to Nvidia GPUs
key_facts: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco on 13 Oct 2026.
He said Cerebras did not have the data centres to handle the capacity OpenAI wanted for its next-generation model.
OpenAI is reported to use Nvidia GPUs for the fast service of its next model.
Cerebras shares fell about 19.5% between 25 Sep and 2 Oct, per BigGo.
Altman said on X on 2 Oct that Cerebras is "a close partner".
Cerebras raised $5.5 billion in an IPO in May and signed a contract with OpenAI worth over $10 billion in January.
quote_evidence: Cerebras Systems' shortage of data centre capacity was a key reason OpenAI turned to Nvidia GPUs to expand services for its next-generation models, co-founder and CEO Andrew Feldman said at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.
OpenAI wanted to significantly scale up supply for its next-generation model based on the success of existing services, but we did not have the data centers to handle that capacity.
why_it_matters_hint: It shows that data-centre space, not only chip speed, decides who wins AI customers.
notes: digitimes paywalled after first sentence; detail from BigGo Finance (which relays a Korean report). Feldman's explanation is the supplier's own account.
